title: baseball-coaster per-game file (games/<season>/<game_id>.json)
$comment:
SEMANTIC EQUALITY: Two files are the same game iff they are deep-equal after deleting `meta` and every `_derived` block. EVOLUTION: MINOR = additive only (new optional property / stat column / `_derived` key); MAJOR = remove/rename/retype/redefine — the only file-invalidating change, the labeled re-parse case. TAXONOMY IS CLOSED: unknown source lines route to `unparsed[]`, never an escape hatch; there is no `x` object and no open `type` enum anywhere. The sole open object is the `_derived` regenerable cache (additionalProperties:true); it and `meta` are excluded from semantic equality. VERSION HISTORY: 1.0.0 initial hybrid (B spine + C grafts). 1.1.0 (additive MINOR) `$defs.substitution.slot` made nullable so a DH-game pitching change (pitcher not in the batting order) is a real substitution event instead of an `unparsed[]` residue. 1.2.0 (additive MINOR) $defs.count and $defs.substitution.player_out made nullable: count=null for a plate_appearance event whose source PBP line carries no count-tail (the historical template), player_out=null for a bare DH-slot entry naming only the incoming player. Ratified by the human via Admiral (issue #30). 1.3.0 (additive MINOR) $defs.outcome.properties.type.enum gains "foul_out" (a foul fly ball caught for an out, fielders populated exactly like flyout/popout) and "strikeout" (a bare struck-out narrative carrying no swinging/looking qualifier, fielders always []) -- no removal/reorder of any existing value. Ratified by the human via Admiral (issue #31). 1.7.0 (additive MINOR) `$defs.player_entry` gains optional nullable `person_id`, the within-season cross-GAME join key: `player_id` is file-local and a synthetic `syn:<side>:<n>` is per-game positional, so joining on it silently mixes people together. Populated from `artifacts/latest/person_map.json` (issue #41 Gap 2). No existing property removed, renamed, or retyped. NOTE: this history has a gap -- 1.4.0 (`box_listed`), 1.5.0 (interference) and 1.6.0 (`infield_fly`) landed without an entry here. 1.8.0 (additive MINOR) `$defs.team` gains optional nullable `franchise_id`, the cross-season club key: `team_id` is reissued every season (0 of 12 multi-season teams keep theirs), so joining a franchise across years on it silently breaks. Minted from the exact team name; registry at `artifacts/latest/team_map.json` (issue #41, team half). No existing property removed, renamed, or retyped. 1.9.0 (additive MINOR) `$defs.player_entry` gains optional nullable `career_id`, the CROSS-SEASON key above person_id: Presto reissues every player id each year, so no source id survives a season boundary. Linked on exact display name + franchise continuity + one-person-per-season, never on name alone (the corpus contains proven same-name different people). Registry and every refused pair: `artifacts/latest/career_map.json` (issue #41 Gap 1). No existing property removed, renamed, or retyped. 1.10.0 (additive MINOR) new top-level `inferred[]` (and `meta.parse.inferred_count`): the disclosure record for every fact `events[]` asserts that its source line does NOT state. Two StatCrew source defects are recovered rather than dropped -- a runner's name written twice where the verb belongs (read as "scored"; the linescore oracle reconciles 54/54 such half-innings when it is counted as a run and 0/54 when it is not) and a pitching change with the incoming pitcher's name blank (filled from the boxscore pitching order, a rule that predicts the named reliever in 8,917 of the 8,991 substitutions that name both). Every such assertion is listed with its rule and its evidence, so a consumer wanting only source-stated facts can drop the events they name. Not added to `required`, so a file written before 1.10.0 stays valid (issue #40).

1.11.0 -- `inferred[].rule` gains `erratum`: an authored, per-line correction to a DEFECTIVE SOURCE LINE, carried in corrections/errata.json and applied to the raw line text before the grammar sees it. It exists so a one-off scorer error never becomes a reason to WEAKEN a general rule. Every rule here is scored corpus-wide against known answers; a phenomenon with N=1 cannot be scored that way, and a rule narrow enough to catch only it is a hardcode wearing a rule's clothes. Admissible only when the phenomenon is essentially unique in the corpus AND other evidence in the same game FORCES the correction; the erratum is pinned to the sha256 of the line it was authored against, so a change in the source detaches it loudly rather than rewriting text nobody reviewed. Additive: `erratum` is a new enum member on an optional field, so a file written before 1.11.0 stays valid (issue #33).

schema_version.description: Semver of THIS schema; the breaking-change gate. MINOR = additive only; MAJOR = remove/rename/retype/redefine. Current: 1.12.0.

game_id.description: Presto boxscore stem; unique within season, e.g. "20260709_h94w".

season.description: Season key (e.g. 2026), not a date range.

status.description: Only finals are written to games/**; literal const.

record_shape.description:
WHICH ORACLES APPLY. `play_by_play` is the ordinary shape: the source published inning panes and `events` holds them. `boxscore_only` is a completed final whose play-by-play the league never published -- a real linescore and a real batting box, and no events at all. Two games are this shape (20250520_iiqj, 20250521_jyjy); both have complete boxscores whose at-bats and hits chain exactly through the AVG the source publishes on every later row.

Required and explicit on every game rather than inferred from `events` being empty. A consumer must not have to know that an absent marker means play-by-play, and the replayer picks its check set from this field -- the five event oracles cannot run on a record with no events, and running them anyway would be five vacuous passes, which is this corpus's oldest failure mode.

date.description: ISO local game date (source pane has no timezone).

players.description: The per-game identity table: keys are file-local pids (the `pid` $def), each value is the player entry whose player_id MUST equal its map key. GRAFT 1's stated identity home.

events.description: The ordered spine; strictly ordered by seq, mixing all event kinds.

unparsed.description: Verbatim source lines the parser could not classify, with location. A non-empty array means events[] is not a complete reconstruction; the file is still published (finals are not blocked on a perfect parse) but flagged.

inferred.description: Facts asserted by events[] that the source line does not state. Empty for a game whose source text was clean. Not in `required`: additive at 1.10.0, so a file written before it stays valid.

pid.description: File-local player id: a 16-char Presto boxscore id, OR a synthetic key `syn:<home|away>:<n>` for a team-site copy where the opponent has no Presto id.

player_ref.description: GRAFT 1: a player reference is an OBJECT (B field names). A future cross-season person_id attaches to the PLAYERS TABLE entry (the identity home), NOT here.

name_raw.description: Raw narrative token, or null when the source region does not name the player (e.g. pitcher-of-record resolved from the lineup).

resolved.description: false only when the last-name token could not be resolved to a boxscore player (e.g. same-last-name teammates); such lines also land in unparsed[].

player_entry.description: Per-game identity home (GRAFT 1's stated home). player_id MUST equal this entry's map key in `players`. `box_listed` (1.4.0) marks a PBP-declared player. `person_id` (1.7.0) is the cross-GAME join key that `player_id` cannot be, and `career_id` (1.9.0) the cross-SEASON key above it; both landed here, as this description always anticipated, not on player_ref.

name.description: Display name from boxscore link text.

last_name.description: Token PBP narrative uses; the join surface.

bats_side.description: Not in source; reserved, null for now.

positions.description: Positions seen in box/lineup this game.

box_listed.description: False when this player appears ONLY in the PBP narrative and has no row in the boxscore's Batters/Pitchers tables -- StatCrew omits an all-zero row for a player who entered but never batted or reached, and (rarely) omits a player who did record a plate appearance. The PBP is authority that they were in the game, so they are admitted to `players`; this flag marks that their identity is PBP-declared, so a consumer never mistakes the absence of box stats for zero stats. Absent means True (every pre-1.4.0 file is boxscore-derived).

person_id.description: WITHIN-SEASON stable person key (1.7.0). `player_id` is FILE-LOCAL: a real 16-char Presto id is stable for a season, but a synthetic `syn:<side>:<n>` is assigned by boxscore ROW ORDER, so the same value means a different person in every game (measured: `syn:away:8` is bound to 99 distinct names in 2026). `person_id` is the id to join on across games. It is the real `player_id` when the player has one, else a minted `person:<16 hex>` derived from (season, team_id, name). NULL means the evidence did not support a link and the player is deliberately unlinked -- an honest negative, never a guess. NEVER a `syn:` value. Scope is one season and one team: PrestoSports reissues every player AND team id each season, so cross-season linkage does not exist here, and a mid-season team change yields one person_id per team. AUTHORITY: `artifacts/latest/person_map.json` -- this field is a materialized copy refreshed at re-parse time, so a game added since the last re-parse may carry null until the artifact is regenerated and the corpus re-parsed. Absent means unknown (every pre-1.7.0 file).

career_id.description: CROSS-SEASON player key (1.9.0), one level above `person_id`. `person_id` is stable across every GAME of a season and deliberately no further, because PrestoSports reissues every player id each year. `career_id` is the key that spans seasons. Two persons in consecutive seasons are linked ONLY when their display names are exactly equal, that name resolves to exactly one person in EACH season, and they share a franchise (`teams[].franchise_id`). Name alone is NOT sufficient and the corpus proves it: two different `Jack Lynch`es both played in 2024, appearing on the same date for different clubs. Franchise continuity is required because it is the one signal that measurably separates the cases (likelihood ratio ~7 vs ~2 for position overlap, which fires on ~45% of people who are definitively not each other and is therefore unused). The honest cost: a player who CHANGED clubs between seasons is left unlinked, in a singleton career -- a complete answer, not a missing value. AUTHORITY: `artifacts/latest/career_map.json`, which enumerates every refused pair with its reason. Like `person_id`, this is a materialized copy refreshed at re-parse time. Null only where `person_id` is null. Absent means unknown (every pre-1.9.0 file).

franchise_id.description: CROSS-SEASON franchise key (1.8.0). `team_id` is SEASON-LOCAL: PrestoSports reissues it every year, and the corpus proves it exhaustively -- of the 12 teams appearing in more than one season, ZERO keep their `team_id`, and no `team_id` is ever reused. Any multi-season question about a club (park factors, franchise run environment) silently breaks when joined on `team_id`; `franchise_id` is the key that survives. Minted as `franchise:<16 hex>` from the exact team NAME, which the corpus supports: within a season name <-> team_id is 1:1, and no team here has ever renamed. A club that RENAMES would get a new franchise_id and needs an explicit alias -- never an inferred one. A relocated-and-renamed club is NOT linked to its predecessor: nothing distinguishes that from an expansion team, and roster continuity was measured and rejected as a signal (it misidentifies 3 of 21 cases where the answer is already known). Registry and the full continuity record: `artifacts/latest/team_map.json`. Unlike `person_id`, this needs no corpus-level evidence -- it is a pure function of the name in this file, so it is always populated and can never drift. Absent means unknown (every pre-1.8.0 file).

team.description: One side's team. `team_id` is SEASON-LOCAL (Presto reissues it yearly); `franchise_id` (1.8.0) is the cross-season key to join a club on.

source.description: GRAFT 2: competition identity, so a multi-league query never has to guess.

site.description: Host the file was scraped from, e.g. "pioneerleague.com".

linescore.description: The primary oracle. null in an innings array encodes the literal "X" (that half was not batted — walk-off/unbatted).

IP.description: Baseball notation (e.g. "5.2"); kept a string to avoid a lossy float cast.

box.description: Secondary oracle + season-rate context. Keyed by team_id.

substitution.description: B §5 substitution shape, reused in lineups[].substitutions and in the substitution event body.

slot.description: Batting-order slot (1-9), or null = the substitute is not in the batting order (a DH-game pitching change). Added nullable in 1.1.0 (additive MINOR); min/max constrain only the integer branch.

player_out.description: Outgoing player, or null = the historical bare DH-slot-entry shape names no outgoing player. Added nullable in 1.2.0 (additive MINOR).

kind.description: Closed substitution kind. B names "offensive" and "pitching"; "defensive" is the grounded complement.

after_event_seq.description: Ties the sub to its position in events[].

type.description: CLOSED taxonomy (B §6.4). Anything outside this set routes the line to unparsed[] and CI fails until the taxonomy is extended.

modifiers.description: e.g. RBI, SAC, unearned, intentional, unassisted, DP, FC, error. Not a frozen enum.

fielders.description: Fielding chain as position tokens, in order; [] when none.

runner.description: B §6.3 from→to primitive. player_id is a BARE pid (not a player_ref).

cause.description: CLOSED runner-cause taxonomy (B §6.3), the asserted mechanism from the runner clause verb.

earned.description: Per-run asserted flag; present for a scored run.

rbi.description: Per-run asserted flag; present for a scored run.

_derived.description: Regenerable base-out CACHE (B §6.5). CI-stamped by the canonical replayer, NEVER hand-authored, validated against the linescore/box/inning_summary oracles before it may persist. EXCLUDED from semantic equality. New analytic keys accrete here — this is the SOLE object in the schema that carries additionalProperties:true.

seq.description: 0-based global order; the sort key and sub-anchor.

narrative.description: Verbatim source line; the ground truth every structured field derives from.

scoring_play.description: Source rendered this line <strong> (a run scored); asserted flag.

count.description: Balls/strikes at this plate appearance, or null when the source PBP line carries no count-tail (the historical template). Added nullable in 1.2.0 (additive MINOR).

pitches.description: Pitch-result string over the observed alphabet, or null when the source omits it (first-pitch ball in play).

inferred_line.description: A fact events[] ASSERTS that the source line does not state, because the source line is defective and a measured rule concluded what it must have meant. Disclosure, not decoration: a consumer that wants only what the source said can drop every event these entries name. Added 1.10.0 (issue #40).

rule.description: Identifier of the inference rule that fired. `erratum` is not a rule but an AUTHORED per-line correction from corrections/errata.json, admitted only when the phenomenon is essentially unique in the corpus and other evidence in the same game forces it -- see bc_pipeline.errata. Its `asserted` carries the erratum id and the evidence verbatim.

asserted.description: What was filled in, and the evidence for it.

meta.description: Provenance. EXCLUDED from semantic equality — a re-parse by the same parser version reproduces a byte-identical file except this block and every _derived cache.

source_sha256.description: Hash of the fetched HTML; the reproducibility anchor.

derived_replayer_version.description: Which replayer stamped _derived.*; the cache-invalidation key.

allOf.$comment: A boxscore_only record has no events and no unparsed lines by construction -- if it had either, the page had play-by-play and the shape is a lie. Enforced here as well as in parse.parse_game because a record shape that only the parser believes in is one a hand-edit can break silently.

And the converse floor: a play_by_play record with no events and no unparsed lines is 20260809_3555 -- a page describing no baseball that scored as fully validated for the life of the corpus because every oracle passes when handed nothing. parse.parse_game refuses it; this says the same thing about the file.
